title: Digital Record Player
oneLine: I put a Raspberry Pi inside a 1byone turntable so it streams Spotify while the platter still spins real vinyl, with a round screen in the middle showing the album art turning at 33 1/3.

hero.alt: Generated stand-in image for Digital Record Player. Not a photograph of the real build.

intake.question: What is it, in one sentence?
intake.draft: A 1byone vinyl turntable retrofitted with a Raspberry Pi 4 into a self-contained Spotify Connect player. The original motor and platter still spin real vinyl, while a 4 inch round display mounted in the center shows the current album art rotating at 33 1/3 RPM, and a web UI on the network controls playback.

intake.question: Role, timeline, status
intake.hint: Is it running now, and did the knob get finished.
intake.draft: Solo. First commit 27 February 2026, last 23 April 2026, 97 commits, so about two months. Four systemd services in the repo (raspotify, display, control, knob) plus a git post-receive auto-deploy hook to the Pi. NEEDS YOU: is it running in your house right now, and did the physical volume knob get finished or is it still a future feature?

intake.question: What made it hard?
intake.hint: Pick one: power, display, or audio.
intake.draft: Candidates from your own notes: sharing one 12V supply between the motor circuit and the Pi while keeping the motor completely independent of it; driving a 720x720 round display under Wayland and labwc in kiosk mode; and the audio path through the PCM5122 DAC HAT. You have both a diagnose-audio.sh and a boot-optimize.sh sitting in the repo, which tells me audio and boot time each cost you real time. Which was worse?
intake.answer: The turntable motor and the Pi had to share one 12V supply, and the motor could never depend on the computer to run. On top of that the 720x720 round display had to come up under Wayland in kiosk mode, and the audio had to stay clean through the PCM5122 DAC.

intake.question: What did you decide, and what did you reject?
intake.hint: Confirm the motor decision and add anything I missed.
intake.draft: This one is documented and it is good: you hardwired the motor to the original OEM switches off the 12V rail rather than putting it under Pi control, and your notes list a 400W dual MOSFET trigger switch as purchased but not used for exactly that reason. A decision and its rejected alternative, with the leftover part as evidence. Second decision worth naming: Raspotify and librespot for the audio path with a separate Flask app on the Spotify Web API for control, instead of one program doing both.
intake.answer: I hardwired the motor to the original OEM switches off the 12V rail instead of putting it under Pi control. I had bought a 400W dual MOSFET trigger switch and deliberately did not use it. If the Pi hangs, the platter still spins and the record player is still a record player.

intake.question: What number can you put on it?
intake.hint: Parts cost, and boot time before and after.
intake.draft: From the repo: 97 commits, Raspberry Pi 4 8GB, 720x720 round IPS touch display, PCM5122 DAC at 384 kHz / 32-bit with 112 dB SNR, 320 kbps stream, 12V 5A supply through a 5A blade fuse stepped down to 5V, 4 systemd services, Flask on port 8080. NEEDS YOU: total parts cost, and boot time before and after boot-optimize.sh. That before-and-after pair is the number this page wants.

intake.question: What broke, and what did you do?
intake.hint: The slow boot and the silent audio. What actually happened.
intake.draft: boot-optimize.sh and diagnose-audio.sh both exist, which means something was slow and something was silent. Tell me what happened and what fixed it.

intake.question: What media do you have?
intake.hint: Shoot the internals and the video. Tell me when it is done.
intake.draft: NEEDS YOU, and this is the highest priority photo shoot on the whole site: the internals with the Pi and DAC HAT stacked, the 12V wiring and fuse, and above all a video of the platter spinning with the album art rotating on the round screen. That clip is the best piece of media you could possibly have. Your README already contains two ASCII architecture diagrams that should be redrawn properly for the page.

intake.question: What would you do differently?
intake.hint: Two sentences. Not self criticism, a design judgement you would make differently now.
